name: Amphetamine
summary: The one drug here whose half-life you can change by what you eat. A large share leaves the body unchanged in urine, and because amphetamine is a weak base, how much is reabsorbed on the way out depends on urine pH. Acidic urine can cut the half-life to about 7 hours; alkaline urine can stretch it past 20.
mechanism: Enters the neuron through the dopamine and noradrenaline transporters, displaces the monoamines out of their vesicles and reverses the transporter, so the cell leaks transmitter outward. It also weakly inhibits MAO, so what is released is not broken down as fast.

oral.note: The therapeutic route. A slow climb over about three hours, which is why prescribed amphetamine feels nothing like the same molecule taken another way.

insufflated.note: Faster onset and a sharper peak, with the same total exposure spread over a shorter window.

pathways.name: Unchanged renal
pathways.note: A third or more leaves untouched in urine, and this is the fraction that urine pH controls. In acidic urine the molecule stays ionised, cannot diffuse back across the tubule, and is flushed out; in alkaline urine it is reabsorbed and recirculates.

effect_levels.label: Levels associated with marked cardiovascular and psychiatric effects

acidic_urine.note: Acidic urine (high protein intake, vitamin C, cranberry) ionises amphetamine in the renal tubule so it cannot be reabsorbed. The half-life can fall to around 7 hours.

alkaline_urine.note: Alkaline urine (antacids, sodium bicarbonate, some diets) lets amphetamine diffuse back out of the tubule and recirculate. The half-life can exceed 20 hours, and doses stack across days.

risk: Because the half-life is long and dose-dependent, redosing through an evening accumulates into the following day. The level that keeps you awake at 2 am is still substantial at noon.
Sleep deprivation, not the drug itself, produces most of the psychiatric harm attributed to stimulants. Amphetamine psychosis is strongly associated with days without sleep.
The cardiovascular load is continuous while levels are up, which with a 10-hour half-life means most of a day after an evening dose.

sources.text: Beckett AH, Rowland M. Urinary excretion kinetics of amphetamine in man. J Pharm Pharmacol. 1965;17:628-39.
